newsitem.title: UK: Weizman invites Britain's queen to Israel.
newsitem.headline: Weizman invites Britain's queen to Israel.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman said on Wednesday he had invited Queen Elizabeth to visit his country.
Weizman, a guest of the queen at Buckingham Palace, is on a state visit to Britain and extended the invitation on Tuesday evening, when he was guest of honour at a lavish banquet.
"I have done so at dinner last night," Weizman said on BBC radio when asked if he had issued the invitation.
"If she has difficulties politically I will not press the point."
Foreign dignitaries tend to visit both Israel and the Palestinian entity in order to avoid being accused of taking sides.
Officials said the queen looked forward to taking up the invitation at a "mutually convenient time" but indicated a trip to Israel was not imminent.
In his interview, Weizman acknowledged the Middle East process was in trouble but denied it had stalled.
"I don't think it's bogged down. It's not moving as it should be. I am concerned."
But he said Yasser Arafat had achieved more than any other Palestinian leader had managed in the past 50 years.
"I think he realises that and therefore he and we are going to be very careful before the balloon goes up," Weizman said.
Later on Wednesday, Weizman and the queen will be joined by United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan for the unveiling of a memorial in London to Swedish diplomat Raoul Wallenberg.
Wallenberg helped tens of thousands of Jews escape the Holocaust in World War Two while he was serving in Hungary. He later disappeared into the Soviet prison system.
